definition: Using AI across product development — ideation, design assistance, testing, and roadmap analytics.
details: Using AI across product development — ideation, design assistance, testing, and roadmap analytics.

explainer.lead: AI for product development means adding AI assistance to the work of deciding, designing, and checking what a product should become. It can help teams explore more options and interpret development evidence, while people remain responsible for the choices.

tiers.eli5: Imagine building a new kind of backpack with a helper who can quickly suggest ideas, sketch variations, and spot possible problems. You still test the backpack and decide which suggestions make sense. AI can play that helper role throughout product development, not just at the idea stage.
tiers.practitioner: Teams apply AI to customer feedback and product goals for ideation, use it alongside design artifacts to propose alternatives, and use it to generate or analyze tests before summarizing evidence for roadmap decisions. Outputs need human review because plausible designs can be impractical, generated tests can miss real failures, and roadmap conclusions can reflect incomplete or biased data.
tiers.paperLevel: This is a workflow concept rather than a single algorithm: given product-development activities A = {ideation, design, testing, roadmap analytics}, AI supplies candidate outputs or analytical summaries for one or more activities, with human evaluation connecting them. Its usefulness depends on the quality of the input evidence and on independent validation; fluent suggestions and test artifacts are not themselves proof of product value or correctness.

explainer.example: A team planning a note-taking app asks AI to group feature ideas, then uses it to propose a design for searchable folders. It next uses AI to help create tests for searching and renaming folders; after reviewers check the tests and results, roadmap analytics summarize the remaining problems so the team can decide whether search reliability or another feature should come next.

usedIn.name: Software product development
usedIn.detail: Teams can move from feature ideas through design assistance and testing to analysis of roadmap priorities.

usedIn.name: Product design
usedIn.detail: Designers can use AI-generated alternatives as starting points for evaluation and refinement.

usedIn.name: Quality assurance
usedIn.detail: AI can assist with testing work, while reviewers check whether the resulting tests are relevant and valid.

usedIn.name: Product management
usedIn.detail: Roadmap analytics can help product managers interpret development evidence when setting priorities.

explainer.intuition: Product development is a chain of decisions, and AI can assist at several links rather than acting as one automatic product-building machine. Its suggestions become useful only when teams compare them with user needs, design constraints, and test evidence.
howItWorks: Gather product goals, user needs, and other relevant development evidence.
Use AI to generate and organize ideas during ideation.
Apply design assistance to propose or refine possible solutions.
Use AI to support testing, then evaluate the results against product requirements.
Analyze the accumulated evidence to inform roadmap choices and feed priorities into the next cycle.
explainer.whyItMatters: Using the same broad capability across several development activities can connect early ideas with later evidence instead of treating AI as a one-off brainstorming aid. That can widen the set of options a team examines and make testing and prioritization easier to discuss, without removing the need for validation.
misconceptions: It is not a single model or algorithm; it describes AI assistance across a product-development workflow.
It does not mean AI can autonomously decide what customers need or approve its own designs.
Generated tests and roadmap analytics are aids to judgment, not guarantees of quality or product success.
